notes: Do not silently run driver cleaners, privacy tools, uninstallers, or driver installers.
Do not bypass or remove licenses from third-party software.
Where licensing is undesirable, build a native replacement module instead of cloning or bypassing the commercial tool.
Keep benchmark tooling separate from the main app UI, but allow internal benchmark-provider integration.

tools.name: Process Lasso
tools.integrationPlan: Do not require or launch this utility for resident backend operation. Build native scheduler controls for priorities, affinities, I/O priority, and per-game rules.
tools.notes: Do not bypass licensing. Resident governor validation must pass without this utility installed or running.

tools.name: HWiNFO
tools.integrationPlan: Create a separate monitoring section for CPU/GPU/RAM sensors, temperatures, clocks, power, utilization, and logging. Prefer reading HWiNFO shared memory or exported sensors when available.

tools.name: CPU-Z
tools.integrationPlan: Expose as a manual launcher and optionally parse exported reports for RAM type, slots, CPU model, motherboard, and BIOS.

tools.name: GPU-Z
tools.integrationPlan: Keep as optional manual GPU diagnostics if needed for VRAM, PCIe, driver, and sensor checks.

tools.name: MSI Afterburner
tools.integrationPlan: Expose install/launch/profile management. Startup is allowed only after user configures and approves GPU profiles. Do not auto-overclock by default.

tools.name: Display Driver Uninstaller
tools.integrationPlan: Offer a guided driver-clean workflow with restore point, network pause option, safe-mode instructions, and post-clean driver install selection. Never run silently.

tools.name: NVCleanstall
tools.integrationPlan: Use for NVIDIA-only client workflows. Gate by hardware detection. Pair with tested driver recommendations and game tags.

tools.name: NVIDIA Profile Inspector
tools.integrationPlan: Provide manual import/export, NIP catalog, benchmark comparison, and top-five tested profile recommendations. Gate by NVIDIA GPU detection.

tools.name: O&O ShutUp10++
tools.integrationPlan: Use as a reference/manual launcher. Native app should implement only the safe privacy subset with rollback and protected ecosystem rules.

tools.name: WPD
tools.integrationPlan: Use as a reference/manual launcher. Native app should implement validated privacy toggles rather than blindly applying WPD presets.

tools.name: Native Bulk Uninstaller
tools.integrationPlan: Build an in-app bulk uninstaller that enumerates MSI, uninstall registry entries, winget packages, Appx packages, services, tasks, startup entries, leftover files, and orphaned registry keys. Do not clone or bypass Revo licensing.

tools.name: Device Cleanup
tools.integrationPlan: Build a dead-device cleanup module using Windows PnP inventory. Default to preview list, backup/export, then cleanup only disconnected/non-present devices.

tools.name: UserDiag
tools.integrationPlan: Keep as separate diagnostic section. After diagnostics, show a plan recommendation CTA based on CPU/GPU/RAM/storage findings and matching services on rooindustries.com.

tools.name: Autoruns
tools.integrationPlan: Educate and optionally expose as an advanced manual tool. Native app should implement safer startup inventory first.
tools.explanation: Autoruns shows nearly everything configured to launch automatically: Run keys, services, drivers, scheduled tasks, shell extensions, browser helpers, codecs, AppInit DLLs, and more. It is powerful but easy to overdo.

tools.name: Thorium
tools.integrationPlan: Do not include in default workflow.

tools.name: Vesktop
tools.integrationPlan: Do not include in default workflow.

driverStrategy.description: Driver installers are shown only when matching hardware is detected. The app should also detect installed games and show driver recommendations tagged by tested game logos.
driverStrategy.metadataUpdate: allow app-side driver/game metadata updates without rebuilding the app

benchmarkStrategy.description: The app should orchestrate benchmarking internally when needed, but benchmark setup/results should remain in a separate workflow rather than cluttering the main optimizer dashboard.
